correctness.rationale: Induction from the defining Leibniz bracket gives unique D=uH+f(N); the shift-power kernel lemma handles u=0. For nonzero u, conjugation by a truncated unit g(N) removes precisely the non-p-divisible degrees via invertible coefficients uj, and the triangular coefficient map is bijective. Residue modulo p makes all remaining eigenvalues cu and nilpotent blocks powers of a single shift; first-nonzero-coefficient counting yields exact Jordan and rank multiplicities for every q=p^e. All counts sum to q^n. Direct independent matrix-rank and Jordan-kernel computations passed 20 exhaustive finite-field configurations; finite tests do not replace the algebraic proof.
